title: The Crane Who Returned a Kindness
titleJp: 鶴[つる]の恩返[おんがえ]し

sentences.jp: 昔[むかし]、雪[ゆき]の深[ふか]いある村[むら]に、貧[まず]しいおじいさんとおばあさんが住[す]んでいた。
sentences.en: Long ago, in a village deep in snow, there lived a poor old man and old woman.

sentences.jp: ある冬[ふゆ]の日[ひ]、町[まち]へ買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]った帰[かえ]り道[みち]で、おじいさんはわなにかかった一羽[いちわ]の鶴[つる]を見[み]つけた。
sentences.en: One winter day, on his way home from shopping in town, the old man found a crane caught in a trap.

sentences.jp: かわいそうに思[おも]ったおじいさんは、わなを外[はず]して、鶴[つる]を逃[に]がしてやった。
sentences.en: Feeling sorry for it, the old man removed the trap and let the crane go.

sentences.jp: その夜[よる]、二人[ふたり]の家[いえ]に、美[うつく]しい若[わか]い娘[むすめ]が訪[たず]ねてきた。
sentences.en: That night, a beautiful young woman came to the couple's house.

sentences.jp: 「雪[ゆき]で道[みち]がわからなくなりました。今夜[こんや]、泊[と]めていただけませんか。」
sentences.en: "I lost my way in the snow. Could you let me stay the night?"

sentences.jp: 二人[ふたり]は喜[よろこ]んで娘[むすめ]を迎[むか]え、娘[むすめ]はそのまま二人[ふたり]と一緒[いっしょ]に暮[く]らすようになった。
sentences.en: The couple gladly welcomed her in, and she ended up staying on and living with them.

sentences.jp: ある日[ひ]、娘[むすめ]は「布[ぬの]を織[お]りたいので、部屋[へや]を貸[か]してください。でも、決[けっ]して中[なか]をのぞかないでください」と言[い]った。
sentences.en: One day the young woman said, "I'd like to weave some cloth, so please lend me a room. But you must never look inside."

sentences.jp: 三日後[みっかご]、娘[むすめ]が部屋[へや]から出[で]てくると、その手[て]には見[み]たこともないほど美[うつく]しい布[ぬの]があった。
sentences.en: Three days later, when she came out of the room, she was holding cloth more beautiful than anything they had ever seen.

sentences.jp: おじいさんがその布[ぬの]を町[まち]で売[う]ると、とても高[たか]い値段[ねだん]で売[う]れた。
sentences.en: When the old man sold the cloth in town, it fetched a very high price.

sentences.jp: 娘[むすめ]は何度[なんど]も布[ぬの]を織[お]ったが、そのたびに少[すこ]しずつやせていった。
sentences.en: She wove cloth again and again, but each time she grew a little thinner.

sentences.jp: 心配[しんぱい]になったおばあさんは、約束[やくそく]を破[やぶ]って、とうとう部屋[へや]の中[なか]をのぞいてしまった。
sentences.en: The old woman grew worried, and finally she broke the promise and peeked into the room.

sentences.jp: そこにいたのは娘[むすめ]ではなく、自分[じぶん]の羽[はね]を抜[ぬ]いて布[ぬの]を織[お]る一羽[いちわ]の鶴[つる]だった。
sentences.en: What was there was not the young woman, but a crane, plucking out its own feathers to weave the cloth.

sentences.jp: 「私[わたし]はあの時[とき]助[たす]けていただいた鶴[つる]です。姿[すがた]を見[み]られてしまったので、もうここにはいられません。」
sentences.en: "I am the crane you saved that day. Now that you have seen my true form, I can no longer stay here."

sentences.jp: 鶴[つる]はそう言[い]うと空[そら]へ飛[と]んでいき、二度[にど]と戻[もど]ってこなかった。
sentences.en: With those words, the crane flew off into the sky and never came back.

questions.q: What did the young woman ask the couple when she started weaving?
choices: To sell the cloth for a high price
Never to look inside the room
To let her go home after three days

questions.q: Why did the young woman grow thinner?
choices: She was using her own feathers to weave
She was sick from the cold
She worked in town at night
Spring came and it had to fly north
The old man sold all the cloth
Its true form had been seen
